standard.title: Specification for Aluminium Foil Stock
standard.sector: Metallurgical Engineering / Light Metals and their Alloys

sectional_committee.name: Ores and Feed Stock for Aluminium Industry, its Metals/Alloys and Products Sectional Committee

standard.description: This standard specifies requirements for aluminium and aluminium alloy foil stock in the form of cold-rolled coils, designed as feedstock for the downstream manufacture of thin aluminium foil of various gauges. It covers chemical composition, mechanical properties, dimensional tolerances, and general technical delivery requirements.
standard.scope: This standard specifies requirements for aluminium and aluminium alloy foil stock in the form of cold-rolled coils, designed as feedstock for the downstream manufacture of thin aluminium foil of various gauges. It covers chemical composition, mechanical properties, dimensional tolerances, and general technical delivery requirements.

certification.description: Voluntary Quality and Performance Certification. Unlike builders hardware or metal packaging containers which are under strict statutory Quality Control Orders (QCOs), industrial aluminium foil stock under IS 10257 : 1982 is certified on a voluntary basis. Conforming manufacturers are eligible to apply for a BIS license to use the Standard Mark (ISI Mark) under Scheme-I of Schedule-II of the BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018. Compliance is routinely mandated inside public and private sector heavy industrial and metallurgical rolling mill supply contracts. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to industrial raw aluminium coils.
requirements: Every commercial tag or label attached to bundles/coils of aluminium foil stock, along with the accompanying test certificate, must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L).

The foil stock must be manufactured from high-purity aluminium or wrought aluminium alloys (such as designations 19000, 19500, 1200, 1235, or 8011) ensuring low iron, silicon, and copper impurity limits to prevent tearing during high-speed rolling into micro-gauges.
Foil stock must be supplied as continuous, solid cold-rolled coils, wound tightly with uniform tension to prevent telescoping or collapse of the inner core during transit and uncoiling.

Stock is typically supplied in one of the standard tempers as specified by the purchaser (such as O - Annealed or H14 - Half-hard) in accordance with temper standards to ensure appropriate starting ductility.

The surface must be clean, smooth, bright, and completely free from physical defects such as edge cracks, laminations, pinholes, slivers, deep scratch marks, corrosion, or heavy surface oxidation which could cause tearing or localized punctures during foil-rolling.

Wrought test specimens must satisfy mechanical limits (such as ultimate tensile strength and minimum elongation percentage) to ensure the sheet can sustain the severe tensions experienced in high-speed, downstream multi-stand rolling mills.

If any test specimen fails to comply with mechanical or chemical limits, a retest is permitted: two additional samples must be drawn from the same lot. The lot is accepted if both retests pass, and is rejected if either retest fails.
